name: Warpdagger keeps one button: the client's own swap is preserved and its auto-placed copy is dropped (#6875)
contract: #6875 'Warpdagger still cloning on PTR, even deleted Cache folder' is the level-10 form submission of the oldest Runemaster report (#4138, #4820, #5417, #6196, #6618, #6770), and it is level 10 because Spell.dbc makes Warpdagger 500287 a SpellLevel-10 one-member chain. The ability's natural shape: casting Warpdagger throws the dagger and the button flips to Warp (500587, or Echo Return 500272 from Echo Rune 500270); pressing the flipped button teleports you to the dagger and the button flips back. The residue behind the report is the client's own spellbook machinery: the 3.3.5 client prints a chat line for every SMSG_LEARNED_SPELL, SMSG_SUPERCEDED_SPELL and SMSG_REMOVED_SPELL and each of those appends or drops a spellbook row, and the swap used all three - the swap packet dropped the Warpdagger row (a one-spell class tab like the reporter's disappears with it while the dagger is out), the per-travel temporary learn was answered by an SMSG_REMOVED_SPELL ('You have unlearned Warp.' on every clear, including logins and map changes), and the row churn fed the auto-placer that cloned the button. This fix takes the shape the codebase already uses for transform abilities (venomancer-widows-kiss-stays-learned): the return spell is learned exactly once, when travel first needs it, and stays learned forever; travel itself sends no learn and no remove. The swap is a silent server-side temporary spell replacement (Player::SetTemporarySpellReplacement with announce off), and the button flips through SMSG_SET_ACTION_BUTTON_SPELL (0x76A), the server's own 'this button holds this spell' packet the client runs as PickupSpell/PlaceAction - the same flip a player dragging the spell onto the button would produce, with the spellbook untouched. AscensionRunemasterTravel::SweepButtonSwapCopies pre-erases the auto-placer's candidate buttons in the same batch as the swap so no copy can flash, and AscensionRunemasterTravelDropButtonCopies stays as the fallback that erases a copy that still lands while the swap window runs, without touching a second button the player placed deliberately. This scenario pins the whole shape on a level-10 Runemaster whose Warpdagger button the fixture placed at slot 3: the throw flips slot 3 to 500587 while the Warpdagger row and the client's knowledge of it never leave, the return spell is learned exactly once across two round trips, no SMSG_SUPERCEDED_SPELL and no SMSG_REMOVED_SPELL is ever sent, slots 4 and 5 stay empty, the recast teleports to the dagger and the button flips back to 500287 - the report is one extra button per swap, unlearned spam, and a class tab that blinks out while the dagger is out.
